title: Synthesis and stability of high-$T_c$ LaH$_{10\pmδ}$ films at high pressures
authors: Sam Cross, William Thomas, Lawrence Nobbs, Rebecca Nicholls, Oliver Lord, Qian Zhang, Dominique Laniel, Max Gerin, Bjorn Wehinger, Mohamed Mezouar, Xiaojiao Liu, Egor Koemets, Annette Kleppe, Sven Friedemann, Jonathan Buhot
abstract: High-pressure hydrides hold the record for the highest superconducting critical temperatures across all classes of superconductors. Currently lanthanum decahydride, LaH$_{10}$, exhibits the highest critical temperature among binaries, with $T_c \approx$ 250 K at pressures between 140-180 GPa. Here, we report the synthesis of LaH$_{10\pmδ}$ films in two DACs at pressures of 168 GPa and 176 GPa via in situ laser heating of elemental lanthanum films with ammonia borane (NH$_3$BH$_3$) as the hydrogen donor. The high-symmetry fcc lanthanum sublattice (space group $Fm\bar3m$) is resolved using synchrotron X-ray diffraction, with unit cell parameters in excellent agreement with previous studies on bulk samples. We provide confirmation of high-$T_c$ superconductivity in LaH$_{10\pmδ}$ with highest $T_c$ of 247 K at 176 GPa evidenced in electrical measurements. The characteristic suppression of superconductivity is observed in magnetic fields. Furthermore, combined diffraction and electrical measurements reveal remarkable temporal stability of both the crystal structure and the high-$T_c$ superconductivity over the full measurement period of about 300 days post laser heating. Our work establishes film precursors using physical vapour deposition (PVD) techniques as a practical route to hydride formation, opening a pathway toward the controlled synthesis of promising ternary hydrides and the integration of micro-fabricated device geometries in diamond anvil cells.
summary: This work reports the successful synthesis of high-$T_c$ superconducting $	ext{LaH}_{10\pm\delta}$ films using a novel film precursor approach in Diamond Anvil Cells. The researchers confirmed superconductivity with $T_c$ near 250 K and, critically, demonstrated that both the crystal structure and the superconducting state remain stable for hundreds of days post-synthesis. This establishes a practical route for creating and studying high-pressure superconductors.
main_problem: The study aims to synthesize, characterize, and assess the long-term stability of high-temperature superconducting hydrides, specifically LaH10, under extreme high-pressure conditions.
main_result: The authors successfully synthesized LaH10 films, confirming a high critical temperature ($T_c \approx 247 	ext{ K}$) and demonstrating remarkable structural and superconducting stability over several hundred days post-synthesis.
method: The research combines in situ laser heating synthesis within Diamond Anvil Cells (DACs) with structural characterization using synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) and electrical transport measurements to probe superconductivity.
model_or_system: The physical system is the high-pressure hydride superconductor LaH10, which is synthesized as thin films on elemental lanthanum precursors within a DAC. Measurements track phase coexistence (e.g., LaH10, LaH9, LaH4) and superconducting properties under sustained high pressure.
key_observables: Critical temperature ($T_c$), upper critical magnetic field ($H_{c2}$), superconducting transition width ($\Delta T_c(B)$), crystal structure (fcc $	ext{La}$ sublattice, $	ext{Fm} ar{3}	ext{m}$), and temporal stability over $\sim 300$ days.
important_parameters: High pressures (168-176 GPa), $T_c \approx 250 	ext{ K}$, and long time scales ($\sim 300$ days).
main_assumptions: The unit cell volume derived from XRD reflects the fcc $	ext{La}$ sublattice, which may not fully capture the stoichiometry of the entire hydride phase.
figures_summary: Figures detail XRD patterns showing phase distribution, spatial X-ray mapping of different hydride phases, and time-dependent measurements of $T_c$ and structural parameters.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure detailing the synthesis method (PVD precursors in DACs), structural confirmation via XRD, measurement of superconducting properties ($T_c$, $H_{c2}$), and finally, a long-term stability assessment over months.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the study of high-$T_c$ superconductivity in novel materials under extreme conditions touches upon strongly correlated electron physics, which is a major area of interest for theoretical condensed matter physicists.
